claims.text:
21. deep-tree-memorises

Target / packet: ai-deep-tree-memorises · C2. Prerequisites: ai:decision-tree-splits, ai:overfitting.

Nearest / distinct payoff: decision-tree-splits → which-question-splits. A tree split improves training fit; this explicit deeper tree memorizes alternating labels while held-out outcomes can reverse its ranking.

Finite primary model: Four training rows x=[0,1,2,3], y=[0,1,0,1]. Deep interval tree splits at.5,1.5,2.5 and memorizes 4/4; stump at 1.5 with constant leaf 0 tie policy gets 2/4. Held-out x=[.4,1.4,2.4,3.4], ground truth[1,0,1,0] makes deep 0/4, stump 2/4.

Countercase and mathematical boundary: Heldout ground truth[0,1,0,1] instead makes deep 4/4. Training fit alone does not determine generalization; declared heldout labels are not generated by an unstated physical process.

Predict and recall transfer: Predict whether training 4/4 forces heldout success; recall alternative ground truth reverses conclusion.

Required observable evidence: Expose tree interval rule and separate heldout labels after commit; no claim deep trees always fail.

Source obligation: Declared local finite model. Exact results require independent arithmetic reproduction; this construction supports no real-model performance or universal improvement claim. Method-source obligations remain as listed in the acquisition record below.
